description:
FILED s463f (Fable review of AU/#960, 2026-09-01).  Pre-existing: identical on 6e6f191 and on AU's tree (probe scratchpad probes/au960b.pl, perl 5.40.3):
    my $r = { m => "abcabc" }; $r->{m} =~ /c/g;  print pos($r->{m});   perl 3   PCL undef
    my @a = ("zzz");          $a[0] =~ /z/g;    print pos($a[0]);     perl 1   PCL undef
    my %h = (p => "abc");      $h{p} =~ /b/g;    print pos($h{p});     perl 2   PCL undef
  while the same shapes WORK in the two ways that matter most:
    pos($h{p}) = 1; print pos($h{p});                                 1 (the #960 write path)
    while ($h{k} =~ /x/g) { ... }                                      terminates after 2, like perl (probes/posloop.pl)
    my @m = ($h{k} =~ /x/g);                                           2 elements, like perl
  So the /g match DOES keep a position for its own loop, but under a key the pos() read does not use: *p-match-pos* is keyed by BOX identity (task #960's note), the loop's `=~` target is whatever box the element's `=~` lowering hands do-regex-match, and `pos($h{p})` now reads through p-gethash-box -- two boxes for one element, or a raw string keyed by identity on one side.  Discriminating measurement (5 min): `./pl2cl` the two statements and compare the target FORM of the `=~` with the argument form of the `pos` call; then check whether p-gethash-box PROMOTES the element (a fresh box replacing the raw slot) after the match already keyed the old one.

WHY IT MATTERS: `pos()` after a /g match on an element is the idiom for tokenizers over `$self->{buf}` (`while ($self->{buf} =~ /\G.../gc) { ... pos($self->{buf}) }`) -- Text::CSV_PP's `pos($c->{tmp})` was #960's own example.  A wrong pos is a silent wrong.

BAR: the four element kinds vs perl after a /g match, after a failed /g (pos resets), and with /gc (pos kept); the posloop.pl rows unmoved; Pl/t/match-vars-01.t rows inverse-verified; a `cl/` change runs the full sweep (every m//g).  Region: do-regex-match target keying + the element `=~` lowering -- correctness slot, round 21 pool.
subject: pos(ELEM) reads undef right after `ELEM =~ /x/g` for every aggregate element kind ($h{k}, $a[0], $r->{k}, $r->[0]) -- the /g match records its position under a different key than the pos() call reads
